# Hermes Agent: Onboarding & Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Welcome to **Hermes Agent**! This guide covers essential concepts, common setup workflows, configuration patterns, and troubleshooting tips.

---

## 1. Installation & Environment

### Platform Support
- **Windows:** Tier 1 native support is available via the official PowerShell installer (`install.ps1`). WSL2 is only needed if you want the Web Dashboard’s embedded browser terminal pane (which requires a POSIX PTY).
- **Docker & NAS Deployments:** Docker images provide multi-arch support (`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` for Apple Silicon / Raspberry Pi). For NAS hosts (UGOS Pro, Synology, unRAID) with bind mounts, pass `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) environment variables to avoid `[Errno 13] Permission denied` errors on `/opt/data/config.yaml`.
- **Termux (Android):** Detected automatically during setup via `scripts/install.sh`, using the `.[termux-all]` dependency group and Android-compatible temporary storage paths.

### Updates & Maintenance
- Run `hermes update` to pull the latest releases.
- *Note on updates:* If the Node.js step seems slow or paused, it is typically downloading browser binaries (Camofox) in the background.

---

## 2. Model Providers & Authentication

### Local LLMs (Ollama, LocalAI)
- **Small Models (4B–9B) Running Slow:** Hermes sends the entire tool schema (~45 tools) on each turn. Small models can struggle with token throughput. To optimize:
  - Disable unused tools: Run `hermes tools` and toggle toolsets off.
  - Set `terminal.backend: local` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to remove container overhead.
  - Use 32B+ models or faster quantizations for tool-heavy workflows.
- **Provider Conflicts:** If Hermes defaults to cloud providers despite local settings, avoid `provider: auto`. Explicitly set `provider: custom` and your `base_url`:
  ```yaml
  model:
    default: ollama/qwen2.5:7b
    provider: custom
    base_url: http://localhost:11434
  fallback_providers: []
  ```
- **Vision Support for Custom Endpoints:** For Ollama/local vision models, set `supports_vision: true` in your model configuration to preserve image payloads.
- **Usage Tracking:** Hermes automatically passes `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}` to OpenAI-compatible endpoints so `/usage` token metrics work properly.

### Cloud Providers
- **Ollama Cloud:** Use the built-in `ollama-cloud` provider which routes to `https://ollama.com/v1`.
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Run `hermes setup` to auto-detect `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL` or configure `provider: azure-foundry`.
- **Google Gemini:** Use Google AI Studio API keys (`GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`). Legacy CLI OAuth integrations have been deprecated and removed.
- **Claude Pro/Max vs. API:** An Anthropic API key bills usage per token. To consume Pro/Max subscription allowances instead of API credits, authenticate via OAuth (`hermes login`).
- **Model Routing Policy:** Hermes does not use dynamic per-turn "smart routing" (cheap vs. expensive model tier switching). Explicitly select models via `hermes chat -m <model>`, configure subagent delegation in `config.yaml`, or use `/model`.

---

## 3. Messaging Gateways (Discord, Telegram, Matrix, DingTalk, Weixin)

### Setup & Authorization
- **Interactive Wizard:** Run `hermes gateway setup` to configure platforms interactively (bot tokens, permissions, user IDs) without manual `.env` file editing.
- **Telegram "Unauthorized User" Fix:**
  - `allowed_chats` restricts group chat IDs; it does **not** authorize private DMs.
  - To authorize a Telegram DM user, add their numeric ID to `allow_from`:
    ```yaml
    telegram:
      allow_from: "6614365140"   # Comma-separated user IDs
    ```
  - Alternatively, use the DM pairing flow (DM the bot, obtain the pairing code, and run `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`) or set `allow_all: true`.

### Personas & Multi-Profile Gateways
- **Per-Channel Personas:** Use `channel_prompts` in your platform configuration (supported on Discord, Telegram, Slack, Mattermost) to define custom system prompts per channel ID.
- **Multi-Profile Support:** Multiple independent accounts (e.g., separate Weixin/Telegram profiles) can run simultaneously in one multiplexed gateway process while keeping memories, tools, and credentials isolated.

### File & Media Handling
- **Incoming Files:** Text files, Python scripts (`.py`), and documents sent to Discord/Telegram are automatically injected into the agent context.
- **Outgoing Files & Media:**
  - Matrix sends documents as native `m.file` uploads; Email gateway sends SMTP attachments.
  - MCP image outputs tagged with `MEDIA:<path>` are delivered as native images on Telegram.
  - DingTalk delivers images via Markdown URL syntax (`![image](url)`).

---

## 4. Agent Execution, Autonomy & Memory

### Turn Limits & Persistent Goals
- **Session Turn Limits:** Conversations default to a turn limit (`agent.max_turns: 90`). Override per CLI call with `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`.
- **Autonomous Long-Running Tasks:** For tasks spanning beyond standard turn caps, use persistent goals:
  - Start with `/goal <objective>` (runs the autonomous Ralph loop).
  - If paused by iteration limits, resume anytime with `/goal resume`.
- **Session Continuity:** Gateway interruptions and restarts transition sessions to `resume_pending` rather than clearing history. Use `/resume` to restore past conversations.

### Memory & Custom Personas
- **`SOUL.md`:** Located at `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`. Defines the core persona, tone, and system instructions of your Hermes agent.
- **`USER.md` vs `MEMORY.md`:**
  - `~/.hermes/USER.md` stores user profile preferences, identity, and personal instructions (updated via memory tools with `target="user"`).
  - `~/.hermes/MEMORY.md` stores general learned facts, historical context, and project notes.
- **Memory Providers:** In-tree memory additions are closed. Custom memory backends (like Honcho or YantrikDB) are supported as external plugins under `~/.hermes/plugins/`. Local Honcho connections (`localhost`/`127.0.0.1`) do not require a remote API key.

### Plugins, Custom Tools & Observability
- **Custom Tools:** Rather than editing core files, build personal tools as plugins in `~/.hermes/plugins/` and enable them via:
  ```bash
  hermes plugins enable <plugin_name>
  ```
- **Tracking Skill Usage:** View skill execution metrics and history using `/insights` in chat or the CLI command `hermes insights` (recorded in `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`).
- **Tracing & Observability:** Enable native Langfuse call-chain tracing via `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse` or `hermes tools`.

---

## 5. Web Dashboard & Interfaces

- **Web UI Dashboard:** Start the official web interface by running:
  ```bash
  hermes dashboard
  ```
  This serves the dashboard locally at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`, complete with settings management and an embedded browser chat interface.
- **Security Inquiries:** Report vulnerabilities responsibly via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) or by emailing `security@nousresearch.com`.
